method: One agent classified each bill against the policyengine-us 2.2.2 source. A second agent, told to refute the call, checked it, and disagreements were settled by hand. pe_paths are the parameter and variable files in that source a reform would set or read. Each reason states PolicyEngine's side in our own words. A Fiscal Lab assumption counts as a lever only when a reform can impose it through policyengine-us, such as a stated premium rise on the benchmark premium the credit reads (slcsp). In 2.2.2 the benchmark parameter (state_rating_area_cost) and slcsp_age_0 also feed the Medicaid cost index (medicaid_slcsp_cost_index), so a reform must apply the change where the credit reads the benchmark, or hold Medicaid cost at baseline. The test is whether a reform can apply the assumption as Fiscal Lab states it to an amount PolicyEngine computes, as with a uniform percentage on slcsp. A take-up response fails it: it means choosing which eligible people or units newly enroll, and 2.2.2's take-up flags (on a person, tax unit or SPM unit) have no rate parameter or enrollment model to choose them, so a run would rest on an assignment PolicyEngine does not make. No PolicyEngine number is recorded.

statuses.not_computed: PolicyEngine's levers carry all (full) or most (partial) of the score. A run could be built; none has been.
statuses.pe_gap: The household model has no lever for the provisions that carry the score: for none of them (none), or for only a minority (partial).
